These could be the reasons for your leaf blower malfunction

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If, like me, your lawn is completely covered with fallen leaves, a leaf blower is a must-have garden tool. Not only can they quickly make cleanup a breeze (no pun intended), but they can also save you the back-breaking task of raking up piles of leaves.

So when your reliable leaf blower keeps cutting out unexpectedly right in the middle of a task, this can be frustrating. Rest assured, you are not the only one dealing with this frequent issue.

In fact, all it takes is a few quick checks and troubleshooting steps that will keep your leaf blower running reliably and ensure your lawn stays free of leaves all season. Here's what you need to do when your leaf blower suddenly stops running.

The first thing is to check for clogs, which will only take minutes. Clogging from trapped debris is a common reason both gas- and electric-powered leaf blowers cut out, as it restricts essential airflow.

For gas leaf blowers, simply remove the filter cover and give it a good clean before taking out the filter itself. To clean it, clear away any loose dirt or debris, then use compressed air to blast out any stubborn blockages.

For electric leaf blowers, simply remove debris in the air intake vent and give it a good wipe-down. Once you’ve done that, this should resolve the annoying shut-off issues you have.

If you have a gas-powered leaf blower, your gasoline might be the culprit of blockages that can affect the engine. This is usually the case if you haven’t used your blower for a long time, and the bad gasoline is no longer fit for use.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Fortunately, this is an easy fix — simply drain the old gasoline in a suitable container, install a new fuel filter before refilling it with fresh gas and oil mix. If the problem continues, inspect the carburetor for build-up and spray it clean with a specialized carburetor cleaner. It’s also worth checking the spark arrestor and fuel cap to remove any debris or stubborn grime.

Another top tip is to test the fuel cap to check if it needs replacing. To determine whether the fuel cap requires this, try loosening it slightly and operating the blower. If the machine runs properly while loose but stalls again once the cap is tightened back down, then a new cap is needed.

If you have a battery-powered blower, you may be dealing with a damaged battery. Usually, a faulty battery struggles to keep its proper charge, resulting in your leaf blower constantly cutting out.

Simply swap it out with a spare or new battery to see if this makes a difference to your performance.

Additionally, store your batteries properly in a dry, moisture-free location away from extreme temperatures.

Netflix will release a new documentary, Russell Brand: Open Secret, on Nov. 13. The film, directed by Olivia Isaacs, “charts the story of Russell Brand’s meteoric rise and steep fall following allegations of sexual offenses.”

According to a press release, Open Secret features inside voices and archive footage that offer insight into Brand’s life and the investigation run by U.K. publications the Times and the Sunday Times and their reporters Rosamund Urwin and Charlotte Wace. A short teaser for the film calls Brand a “shapeshifter” and a “grifter,” and explains that the journalists initially didn’t realize their investigation would lead to criminal charges.

Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Nov. 5 following a trial in London. He was found not guilty on two additional counts of rape, as well as one count of attempted indecent assault. The allegations against him were tied to claims made by six women between 1999 and 2009. The actor and comedian was sentenced to 10 years in prison.

Police began investigating Brand in 2023 after multiple women came forward with allegations of assault and abuse in a Channel 4 documentary and the Sunday Times report. Prosecutors first filed five charges against Brand in April 2025, while two additional charges were brought in December.

Following the trial, Brand’s attorney Ian Winter confronted Urwin outside the courtroom, telling her “I hope you are pleased with yourself.” Urwin responded, “I’m pleased justice has been done,” to which Winter replied, “Well, it wasn’t. You fucked it.” Winter later confirmed he had referred himself to the Bar Standards Board.

Urwin explained on a Times podcast that she approached Winter after the verdict because her name had been mentioned during the trial. “I thought he’s talked about me a lot, I’ll go and introduce myself and that is a legitimate thing to do,” she said. “I was surprised to be confronted and spoken to in that way.”

The bulk of Brand’s sentence is tied to the rape charge, for which the judge sentenced him to nine years in prison. Meanwhile, each of the three assault charges carried their own penalty: nine months, 18 months, and eight months. The assault sentences will be served concurrently, but consecutively with the sentence for the rape charge. Trending Stories Sade Are Not Attending Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For Bob Dylan’s Meeting With Pope Leo: People Fixated on the Hood, But the Hands Spoke Volumes Megan Thee Stallion and Daniel Radcliffe Reunite for Season Two of ‘Reggie Dinkins’

Brand will eventually be eligible for parole, but only after serving two-thirds of his sentence. That means he will spend at least seven years behind bars, and, if granted parole, would have to serve the remainder of his sentence under supervision and abiding by specific rules.

The Metropolitan Police are continuing to investigate Brand after several people contacted them with information during and after the trial. “Detectives are assessing this information as part of their ongoing enquiries,” a spokesperson told the BBC.

#3353. Canadian court certifies class action against Apple over Google search deal

A British Columbia Supreme Court judge has certified a class action against Apple over allegations that its search agreement with Google stifled competition and inflated advertising prices. Here are the details.

In recent years, Apple’s deal with Alphabet to make Google the default search engine on Safari has drawn regulatory attention in the US, the UK, and Australia, while related search competition concerns have also come under scrutiny in the EU and Japan.

While the details of each investigation differ, they all raise concerns about the impact of Google’s dominance in search, as well as the extent to which its agreements with other companies might be limiting competition.

More recently, Apple’s agreement with Google received significant attention during the US Department of Justice’s antitrust case against the search giant, which included testimony from Apple executives Eddy Cue and John Giannandrea. The latter joined Apple from Google in 2018 and led its AI efforts until stepping down earlier this year.

As a result of the US case, a federal judge ruled in August 2024 that Google had illegally maintained its monopoly in online search through anticompetitive agreements, including its deal with Apple.

Now, evidence presented during that trial has become central to a class action against Apple in Canada, which a British Columbia Supreme Court judge recently certified.

The case was initially brought in 2021 by Spark Event Rentals Ltd., an event rental company based in British Columbia. The plaintiff alleged that Apple and Google conspired to limit competition in the search market, allowing Google to charge advertisers artificially inflated prices.

Apple, meanwhile, argued that its agreement with Google was a legitimate distribution arrangement rather than an unlawful conspiracy. The company also maintained that Google was the appropriate defendant, describing itself as an “innocent bystander.”

Interestingly, the lawsuit originally named both Apple and Google as defendants, but the plaintiff later dropped Google from the case following a dispute over an arbitration clause in its advertising contracts.

With Apple now the sole defendant, Justice Thomas has allowed the case to proceed as a class action, finding sufficient grounds to examine whether Google’s payments discouraged Apple from developing its own search engine.

The lawsuit seeks financial compensation for advertisers who allegedly overpaid for Google search ads, and the court has also allowed the question of punitive damages to proceed.

The class action covers Canadian residents who purchased search ads from Google since 2005, when Apple and Google first agreed to make Google the default search engine on Safari in exchange for a share of advertising revenue.

Importantly, the ruling does not establish that Apple engaged in anticompetitive conduct, but simply allows the allegations to proceed as a class action.

The central proposition raised by these pleadings is that Apple could have used its resources and distribution network to enter the search engine market, but chose not to because Google paid Apple billions of dollars in revenue-share payments to make Google the default search provider on Apple products. This arrangement gave Google market power, enabling it to charge supracompetitive advertising prices on search engines.

In my view, this pleads a common purpose to perform an act prohibited by s 45 of the Competition Act, such that it is not “clear and obvious” that the plaintiff has not pleaded an agreement between Google and Apple not to compete in the search engine market.

At one point in his decision, Justice Thomas cites Giannandrea’s testimony and directly quotes Cue’s from the US antitrust trial, before concluding that “this provides some basis in fact, supporting the inference that Apple did not compete with Google in the search engine market because of its Agreement with Google.”

Interestingly, the judge also acknowledges Apple’s objections to the evidence, agreeing that “the plaintiff has cherry-picked evidence to support his case,” but adding that, in his view, “it is appropriate to do so at this stage in the proceedings.”

With the class action greenlit, the case can now move forward toward trial, though no date has been announced yet.

#3351. Elijah Wood Says “Muscle Memory” Kicked In Playing Frodo On ‘The Hunt For Gollum’ Set

Elijah Wood told Deadline tonight that playing Frodo again after more than two decades was “beautiful and surreal and it felt like no time had passed.”

Wood reprised the role earlier this year on director Andy Serkis’ new Middle-earth set tale, The Hunt For Gollum.

The actor has spoken in anticipation of returning to the part, but these may be his first public observations after having done so.

Serkis confirmed yesterday that principal photography for the film has now wrapped.

The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum reunites beloved figures from across Middle-earth, including Ian McKellen as Gandalf, Wood as Frodo and Lee Pace as Thranduil. New actors announced for the film include Anya Taylor-Joy, Kate Winslet, Jamie Dornan and Leo Woodall. Serkis directs and returns as Gollum in the film. Watch on Deadline

“I think it really is a creative ‘getting the band back together.” Wood told Screen Rant before production in January. “It’s very much that core original group getting back together to tell this story that will feel like a really fun exploration of this character that we all love so much.”

Wood spoke tonight about being on set in his costume and hobbit feet again.

“It felt like stepping back into time. You know, looking down…having this sort of muscle memory that I’ve seen these feet this way. I know this wardrobe. And that feeling is so wild. It’s so transportive. Suddenly 27 years are gone and you’re back in it again.”

Elijah Wood on returning as Frodo for ‘The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt For Gollum’ pic.twitter.com/srVYx98Ud4

The Hunt for Gollum follows Aragorn’s perilous quest to capture Gollum before the creature can reveal the One Ring’s location to Sauron. The story, much of it developed from Tolkien’s footnotes, is set between the events of The Hobbit and The Fellowship of the Ring.

Last month, Serkis posted a video slideshow from the set. One of the final images shows what looks to be Wood as Frodo entering Bilbo’s hobbit house. You can watch it below.

Warner Bros. Pictures will release The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum worldwide on December 17, 2027.

#3349. Rolling Stone Essentials 2027

From fresh takes on familiar staples to unexpected game-changers and brands that simply have it, these are the companies and products earning our ultimate stamp of approval.

From fresh takes on familiar staples to unexpected game-changers and brands that simply have it, these are the companies and products earning our ultimate stamp of approval

ASUS had a big year of releases, and while a lot of the attention went to the flashy dual-screen models the brand unveiled, their traditional laptop releases were worth paying attention to as well. The Zenbook A16 has a lightweight design without sacrificing screen size, and the dazzling OLED display also features a touchscreen. You get more ports than you typically expect on a modern laptop, including two USB-C ports, a USB-A port, an HDMI port, and an SD card reader. Overall, it’s a powerful laptop that suits a range of use cases.

The Pixel Watch does what few smartwatches have been able to pull off — look like an actual watch. With a domed display, the face doesn’t call attention to the fact that it’s a screen, and the latest Pixel Watch 5 packs in all of the features you need, including health tracking and sleep tracking, plus features you want but hopefully won’t need, like car-crash detection and SOS satellite communications.

Best known for their affordable TVs, TCL has been raising the bar to become one of the best all-around TV brands, with the right combination of innovation, quality, and value. Their SQD mini-LED TVs deliver greater brightness and contrast, with up to 3,000 peak nits for a vibrant display even in bright rooms.

Boox has proven that an e-reader can be more than an e-reader. The brand’s versatile e-ink gadgets run the gamut from phone-sized e-readers to large note-taking tablets. Because they run Android, you can download a versatile suite of apps. Their latest device is the itty-bitty Picco, which is roughly the size of a playing card. With support for ePub and a microSD slot, you can take a variety of file types to read on the go.

Skylight bills itself as a family-oriented product, designed to help corral kids’ schedules and organize chores. But it’s surprisingly useful in child-free households, or even at the office. As editors who tend to find appointments and obligations sneaking up on us, the easy at-a-glance organization makes it easy to figure out what we have going on that day, and it syncs easily with a variety of calendar apps. The subscription unlocks more, but you can still do a lot with the free tier.

SwitchBot makes a dizzying array of smart home products, with wide support for a range of platforms. The smart locks let you use everything from fingerprints to facial recognition, while the cameras are a more affordable alternative to other tech brands. You can also build a whole-home ecosystem with accessories like smart window shades and lighting. With so much smart tech, it’s easy to forget SwitchBot started as just a Bluetooth button-pushing gizmo.

XGIMI makes projectors for every kind of enthusiast, from home theater pros to on-the-go gamers, and this year marked some major releases from the brand. There was the cinematic Titan Noir Max, the space-saving short-throw Aura 3 Max, and the ultra-portable battery-powered Vibe One. Across price and class, XGIMI has been delivering stylish design, excellent picture quality, and user-friendliness.

It’s rare to see a headphone brand actually shake up the big players, but Daisy proved to be one of the buzziest if-you-know-you-know brands thanks to its stellar design. The aluminum accents set it apart from the all-plastic construction of most headphones, but they look a lot more expensive than they are. Tactile controls make for a refined experience, while solid sound and noise-canceling hold up the performance end of the equation.

PSB’s iQ bookshelf speakers are some of the most stylishly contemporary speakers we’ve seen, with a unique design that puts the bass driver on top of the tweeter. The speakers also connect to each other wirelessly, adding greater flexibility in where you can plug them in. As for listening to music, they support BluOS for multiroom audio, and they have inputs for HDMI eARC, RCA, optical, USB-C, and USB-A, making them flexible and versatile.

Year after year, Q Acoustics proves to be a hi-fi brand that enthusiasts keep coming back to. Their latest release is the 3040C floorstanding speakers, which are headed to the U.S. market soon. They’re slimmer and sleeker than most tower speakers, but they don’t compromise on sound, with clear highs and distortion-free bass. Eye-catching yet unobtrusive, they’re also a stylish addition to any living room or home theater.

Nanu is all about taking a less-is-more approach. The brand currently offers two products, a mechanical counter and an alarm clock. We’ve been using the Arc alarm clock in our daily routine, and it might be the low-tech answer we’ve been waiting for. It has a sturdy metal build and a pleasing retro look, but the digital alarm adjustment is more precise than most analog alarm clocks. Yes, it’s pricey, but after accidentally breaking a series of cheap digital clocks (we’re not morning people), we’re glad to have something that feels built to last.

I’ve been lucky enough to test a lot of impressive audio products, but it’s rare to find one that truly blows me away. KEF’s R11 Meta fit the bill, delivering an exceptional amount of detail, even in rooms that are less than ideally set up.

As for sound, each speaker gets plenty loud thanks to the four bass drivers. There’s also an aluminum mid-range driver that houses a 1″ vented aluminum dome tweeter, which means the bass doesn’t overwhelm the mids or highs. Given their size and low impedance rating, you’ll want an appropriately powerful amplifier to power them.

They’re strikingly good-looking and are available in glossy black or white finishes, or more classic walnut. They are also, it should be noted, gigantic; getting them home and unboxing them was its own odyssey.

It won’t shock you that the R11 Meta speakers are an investment. They’re $3,500 (for one speaker; the pair will set you back $7,000), so I could hardly blame KEF for making sure the pair was returned promptly after I tried them. I might not be in the requisite tax bracket to justify buying these permanently, but they’ve earned a spot on my wishlist. —Jonathan Zavaleta

Beyond Yoga takes activewear well past the workout. Sure, the brand has gear for just about every activity you can think of, but it also has seriously comfortable pieces you’ll want to change into after you finish your reps. Everything they make is top-notch, right up to the hats. And the best part? The price point gives the other guys some serious competition.

Cozy Earth might be famous for its beautiful bedding, but the comfort giant has another home essential on lock: loungewear. From ridiculously soft pajamas and matching sweat sets to slippers for the whole family, the brand has staying-in style down to an art. The lineup is so good, it might just give those bestselling sheets a run for their money.

What makes good denim? In our minds, the best jeans should wrap modern, comfortable design, high quality, and sustainability in a package that most consumers can afford. If you need an example of top-tier denim production, look to DL1961. The New York City label makes all of its denim in a family-owned factory using premium materials, and their considerate approach comes through in the final product. They’ve also got a great rotation of washes and fits, ensuring something for nearly every personal preference.

Buck Mason is arguably the biggest menswear success story of the past decade. Their pieces would look great in any era over the last seventy-odd years, and they feel like they’ll last into the next couple of decades at least. If we were building a menswear wardrobe, Buck Mason would be our first stop.

Spanx has just about every corner of the women’s wardrobe covered, from the bottom up. Its shapewear is a total game-changer, its undergarments offer support where it counts, and its clothing is as flattering as it is comfortable. From office-ready workwear to essentials for a night out, Spanx has everything you need to wear, both underneath it all and on the outside.

It takes a licking, keeps on ticking, and we can’t stop recommending it. Timex has been in peak form for the last several years, putting out achievement-inspired and collaborative pieces that are just plain cool. And their watches just happen to be very affordable, too. Their catalog is very deep, so almost everyone will find something they like, whether it’s the Nineties-inspired Intrepid x Dimepiece, the Bespoke Post x Timex Heritage 66 dive watch, or the slick Cavatina Mini dress watch.

There’s a mountain of outerwear out there, but not every brand knows how to balance comfort, style, and performance. Free Country does all three. Founded in the Nineties, the brand makes best-selling layers that can go as rugged or refined as you want, whether you’re tackling the outdoors or just sipping cocktails on a patio.

Swimwear is a tricky art: It needs to be stylish, flattering, comfortable, and built to perform. Vilebrequin checks every box. Born in Saint-Tropez, the brand brings bold prints, endless silhouettes, and seriously standout designs to the beach. It’s the kind of swimwear that will completely change how you feel about shopping for bathing suits in the first place.

Footwear is a tough space to crack, but Alohas has pulled it off. After a decade in business, the Barcelona-based label has established itself as one of the most reliable sources of high-quality shoes that are on-trend, sustainable, and reasonably priced. That’s a rare combination. Best of all, they produce footwear in categories from sneakers to dress shoes that all rival much pricier designer pairs.

Ana Luisa has mastered the art of having it all (at least when it comes to jewelry): Quality, innovation, and plenty of personality. It’s no surprise that one of the co-founders previously worked with some of the world’s best-known designer brands before taking what he learned and turning it into something special. From fun, customizable costume items to finer pieces worth gifting (and keeping for yourself), Ana Luisa makes jewelry shopping feel anything but ordinary.

There’s nothing quite like the thrill of finding a hidden gem at a thrift store, but when you don’t have a free Sunday to spend digging through Brooklyn racks, ThredUp brings the hunt straight to your couch. Shop hundreds of designers and beloved brands, or sell pieces from your own closet. It’s secondhand shopping without the noise.

How do you pack for a safari? Well, if you’re toting the Peak Design Travel Duffel, the answer is pretty simple. I lugged the lightweight carry-on to Africa this year, and it held up to everything from a sudden rainstorm in an open SUV to a sandstorm in the Serengeti. That’s thanks to Peak Design’s proprietary “Versa Shell” material, which is fully weatherproof and reinforced to withstand wear and tear (scrapes and scuffs were also easily wiped off with a damp cloth). The practical thinking extends to the duffel’s storage capabilities, with two internal mesh pockets for organization and four external zip pockets for easy access. Thoughtful details abound, like flaps over the zippers to prevent water from getting in, and a waterproof bottom liner that helps the bag sit flat for easy packing. A padded shoulder strap and two top handles offer multiple ways to carry the duffle, whether you’re running to make a connection or tossing the bag in a bush plane. Peak Design offers multiple colorways, but the all-black duffel is minimalist and modern-looking, offering a bag that’s as streamlined as your travels. —Tim Chan

There are hundreds of face washes out there, but Pour Tous gets our ultimate seal of approval for keeping things simple. No need to hunt down a specialty cleanser for your skin type or concerns: This one is made for everyday use, morning and night, with an affordable price tag that’s just as refreshing.

PROVEN is the Goldilocks of moisturizers: Not too heavy, not too light, but just right. Its creams glide on without feeling caked or leaving behind an overpowering scent, while helping keep dry, cracked skin at bay. From eye cream to night cream, the lineup has your hydration needs covered.

Think you can skip serum in your skincare routine? Think again. With so many formulas competing for your attention, TimeSavvy makes the decision a whole lot easier. Its dermatologist-developed makeup combines everyday skincare with sun protection, making it an easy addition to your “get ready with me” routine.

Vacation makes the kind of sunscreen you actually look forward to wearing. Of course, you should always take your SPF seriously, but the brand makes reapplying feel less like a chore and more like part of the fun. Between its incredible scents and seriously adorable packaging, even a New York sidewalk can feel like a tropical escape.

Blue Lagoon Skincare comes all the way from Iceland (yes, that Blue Lagoon), and its products make you feel like you’ve discovered a little piece of magic. The eye cream is a standout, helping visibly reduce the look of dark circles and puffiness. Sometimes the best beauty secrets come from the middle of the North Atlantic. Luckily, no passport is required.

SEEN proves that good haircare should do more than just look pretty on your bathroom shelf. Its products help make hair look and feel noticeably better, while its customizable bundles let you build a routine around exactly what your hair needs. No guesswork, no overcomplicated regimens — just really good haircare in seriously sexy packaging.

Most hairstyling brands are slick with no substance, but Forte Series eschews hype in favor of results. The grooming brand’s line of everyday products includes refreshing texture sprays, volumizing shampoos, gentle hair oils, and quick-fix styling aids that address everything from frizz to flatness. We like the molding paste, which offers a flexible hold, matte finish, and no sticky residue. From hair repair to hair care, Forte Series offers the best products to help you lock in your look.

The name might be French, but Nécessaire is an American-founded brand that has turned everyday self-care into something special. A cult favorite with celebrity appeal, its body washes leave skin feeling like you’ve just stepped out of a five-star spa. The lingering scents are just an added plus.

Salt & Stone tapped Role Model for a buzzy campaign in 2026, but the deodorant brand has long been a fan favorite thanks to its aluminum-free formula, minimalist packaging, and fresh and modern scents. Skin-nourishing ingredients keep your underarms soft and supple, and 48-hour protection means you’re covered, even if you skip a swipe. Whether you’re headed to a sweaty concert or under pressure at work, consider the brand an essential pit stop.

Gillette dared to go where few shaving brands have gone before with the launch of its GilletteLabs Body Razor, and dare we say – it makes the cut. The razor delivers a smooth and gentle glide, with evenly-spaced blades that won’t get caught in your hair (or worse). A grippy handle and flexible head allow you to reach even the most sensitive areas with ease, and it’s smooth sailing from there. Gillette has long been the first choice for our face, but as grooming routines get personal, it’s now the best razor brand for our bodies too.

Braun is making a compelling case to bring the electric shaver back, thanks to its NEVO 11000c. Made in Germany with stainless steel construction, the handheld trimmer is as durable as it is precise, with a smart processor designed to adapt in “real time” to your facial hair density. What you get: An ultra-smooth and comfortable shave, with a flexible head that hugs the dimples and crevices of your face without irritation. When you’re done, plug the shaver into the NEVO Care System dock, which automatically cleans and charges the blades. This is advanced shaving made simple.

Fragrance is deeply personal, but OneKind makes finding your next signature scent feel like the best kind of shopping spree. Its clean products offer plenty of options to suit different tastes and vibes, making it nearly impossible to settle on just one.

Medicube may have serious celeb backing (see everyone from Kylie Jenner to Lisa from Blackpink), but the Korean skincare brand is also delivering some serious results with its Booster Pro X2. The handheld device is a miracle worker for your skin, helping to tone and tighten, while adding brightness and bounce. Use it on its own, or pair it with your skincare products (or over a sheet mask) to boost absorption. The celeb skincare secret is out, and getting that Hollywood glow at home has never been easier.

Spend a few days basking under the glow of a Helio Cure red light panel and a few things become apparent: You’ll feel more awake and alert, while your skin starts looking more refreshed. Helio Cure’s clinical-grade products are said to deliver the industry’s highest density of therapeutic red light wavelengths, which work to help boost collagen production, improve skin tone, and soothe inflammation, while easing sore muscles for post-workout recovery. Easy to use and backed by science, Helio Cure will have you seeing yourself in a whole new light.

Amid concerns over microplastics, it’s understandable that many are looking twice at the tools they use in the kitchen. Some appliances are easier to go plastic-free than others, which is why Caraway’s new coffee maker is so exciting. The brand removed plastic from all of the parts that touch water or coffee. There’s a glass carafe and water reservoir, while the water moves through stainless steel pipes. But that only goes so far if the coffee doesn’t taste good, and Caraway’s coffee maker meets Golden Cup Standards.

We’ve tested plenty of vacuums in our time, and few hold up quite like Shark. Its prices are competitive, but the real selling point is performance: Whether you’re tackling a massive spill or trying to regain control of the pet hair that’s taken over your home, Shark gets the job done. It’s the kind of investment that keeps paying off, year after year.

Air purifiers are an essential part of a healthy home, yet they’re often the most overlooked. If you need a place to start, make it Molekule. Its sleek designs won’t become an eyesore in your living room, while its impressive technology works behind the scenes to help keep your surroundings cleaner. Consider it a breath of fresh air in more ways than one.

Helix mattresses have changed the way we think about getting a good night’s rest. With options backed by sleep experts and designed around different sleeping positions and habits, the brand makes finding your perfect match easier than ever. Not sure what kind of sleeper you are? Its mattress quiz takes the guesswork out of choosing, so you can leave the sheep counting behind.

Macy’s carries hundreds of products, but its own Hotel Collection deserves a moment in the spotlight. From sheets to comforters and bedspreads, the brand brings a posh experience to your bedroom. Think thoughtful craftsmanship, beautiful design, and the kind of luxe lineup that makes getting out of bed feel like a missed opportunity.

Furniture can sometimes feel old and tired, but Sundays is giving everyday essentials a much-needed glow-up. Its couches, beds, chairs, and more feel decidedly modern while still managing to be timeless. And if you just want to upgrade one piece rather than your entire collection (although you might be tempted), everything blends effortlessly with what you already own. Give Sundays a round of applause for making furniture fun again.

A few of our editors own a Rocco fridge, and they all agree: It’s guaranteed to make guests stop and stare. And for good reason. This is no run-of-the-mill beverage cooler; Rocco is a statement piece with room for everything from wine and beer to your favorite nonalcoholic seltzers. It even features smart technology that lets you control the temperature and see what’s inside, though guests might be too busy admiring its good looks to notice.

Riedel helped define how wine should be experienced, and 270 years after it was originally established, Riedel glassware is still the best way to serve any liquid. All of its offerings, from wine glasses to tumblers to decanters, are purpose-built to make your drinks taste better and look better when you serve them.

You might never open your own pizzeria in Brooklyn, but Ooni somehow makes you feel like you’re running the place from behind the counter. The pizza oven brand offers options for everyone, from seasoned pros to first-time pie makers. Its products are easy to use and compact enough to leave plenty of room for all your favorite toppings.

Meraki made a big splash with its Gen 1 espresso machine in 2024. It won over reviewers (us included) with a brilliant semi-automatic functionality, a suite of barista-level features, and a very handsome, compact design. Earlier this year, Meraki launched the Gen 2 version, which adds a 45-step grind range to handle almost any beans and a dual-stage water distribution design, among other new features. In other words, Meraki made an already amazing machine even better. And, maybe just as impressive: Meraki didn’t change the price tag, maintaining a very impressive level of value for an espresso machine this advanced. —Oscar Hartzog

A smartwatch is a great way to meet your fitness goals — until it becomes a distraction. The Fitbit Air has the same appeal as other screen-free fitness trackers, but with a slimmer, more attractive look. The subscription adds more features like an AI-powered fitness coach, but there’s a lot you can get done without it, including workout and sleep tracking. The low-profile bracelet design also makes it a great option where rings or watches might get in the way.

Although the two big guys get most of the running world’s attention, we’re crowning Brooks the best running shoe brand on the market right now. We’ve tested Brooks shoes in all categories, from distance shoes to speed runners to trail shoes, and all of them deliver the same reliable performance, comfort, and long-term durability.

Alo makes great apparel and accessories, but its workout essentials deserve just as much praise. Its premium yoga mats, better known as Warrior Mats, are a standout, with a range of colors to complement your style. They’re also made with easy-to-clean materials, so keeping your mat fresh between sessions is simple — and you can roll it out time and time again.

Hyperice makes massage guns that are perfect for chilling after you’ve given it your all on the trails (or the treadmill), but the brand isn’t afraid to think beyond traditional recovery tools. Its unexpected collaborations, including vibrating sandals designed with Nike, caught our attention for all the right reasons. But if you want to stick to the basics, Hyperice’s massage guns are a pretty great place to start.

After rebranding from Theragun to Therabody, the wellness brand has continued to expand beyond fitness massagers. Their latest tech includes face massagers, red-light therapy devices, and skincare tools, with gadgets that go beyond just being for athletes. But they still excel at making fitness-focused gear, from heated massage guns to compression boots that deliver quick relief.

Lemme might be best known for its co-founder, Kourtney Kardashian Barker, but we’re here to argue that the products deserve their flowers, too. Its lineup of gummies covers everything from sleep and gut health to intimate wellness, so rather than wandering endless supplement aisles trying to figure out what your body needs, you can find targeted options all in one place. They’re tasty enough to make sticking to the suggested serving size the real challenge.

LARQ water bottles may run on the slightly pricier side, but once you see what they can do, they’re worth every penny. Some models come packed with futuristic features like built-in filtration, app connectivity to help track your daily H2O intake, and even self-cleaning technology, while others earn high marks for their sleek looks and durability. Whichever option you choose, it’ll make you think twice about all those other water bottles collecting dust in your cabinet.

Many home gym systems try to invent a new product that supposedly delivers full workout, but Force USA takes a different approach. The brand’s Cornerstone All-In-One setups combine all the most effective elements of a gym into one durable structure. The crown jewel is the C20, a multifunction structure built around a power rack that supports dozens of exercises — all just like the ones you’d hit in the gym. In other words, it’s actually like having a gym at home.

Sometimes scrolling through social media can send you further into your own head, but Headspace is here to do the exact opposite. For as little as $12.99 a month, a subscription gives you access to everything from guided meditation exercises to online therapy, helping you feel a little better with just a few taps.

FitOn turns your phone into a comprehensive wellness guide. The app delivers a massive library of guided workouts, including classes by professional and celebrity coaches, plus content to improve your nutrition and mindfulness practices. Whatever your fitness goal, FitOn is a great way to achieve it (and you don’t even need to leave the house).

Sorting through supplement brands is a mammoth undertaking, but Transparent Labs makes things easier. As the name suggests, the brand is all about candidness, making their formulas as clear and available as possible. They also employ extensive third-party testing and provide Certificates of Analysis (COAs) and certifications from Informed Choice, which give deeper insight to the products than almost any other supplement brand.

Finding Soul is almost as relaxing as taking one of their CBD products. The Austin-based brand offers exceptionally clean cannabis products that are organically grown in the U.S. and subject to thorough third-party testing. They’re also presented in stylish, approachable packages that let consumers know exactly what they’re getting.

LELO has its finger on the pulse — or should we say, button — when it comes to what people actually want from their pleasure products. Its lineup includes sex toys for both men and women, alongside supplements, lubricants, and essentials like condoms, so you can stock up on everything you need without ever having to set foot in a sex shop.

Some products stop you in your tracks, and for me, it was the ridiculously good-looking Porsche x WonderFold Stroller Wagon. I couldn’t get over how something so luxurious could also be so practical, so naturally, I had to take it for a spin. There’s just one small detail: I don’t have kids. Luckily, my brand-new niece was available for a test drive (she didn’t exactly have a say in the matter). At least she’ll have some pretty incredible throwback photos to post one day. From the premium leather seats and headlights to the Porsche-inspired details, spill-proof mat, and upgraded wheels, this stroller doesn’t skimp on the extras. Is it technically for the baby? Absolutely. But let’s be honest: It’s also for the parents who wouldn’t be caught dead in a minivan and have no intention of starting now. —Alexis Mikulski Ruiz

The streaming world has settled down now that most major studios have launched their own services. The best streaming services right now are ones that are comprehensive and customizable. DirecTV wins at both. It offers a wide range of packages for different budgets and viewing needs, and all of them offer a great lineup of live TV channels. Plus, most of them also include complimentary subscriptions to other streaming apps like ESPN Unlimited, HBO Max, Hulu, and Paramount+. If we could only pick one streaming service to use in 2027, it would be DirecTV.

For sports fans, YouTube TV is an exceptional offering. The live-TV streamer offers two packages that both carry dozens of channels, including all major networks showing sports. It also boasts one of the best user interfaces of any live-TV streaming service, and its prices are very reasonable for how much content you get.

Hulu + Live TV delivers all the best content in one package. You get more than 100 live-TV channels, plus all the on-demand content from Hulu, Disney+, and ESPN Select (upgrade for ESPN Unlimited as well). All of this comes in at under $100, making it a great value for anyone looking to keep up with sports, news, and new series.

In terms of original content, HBO Max has yet to be beaten. The platform has one of the deepest libraries of shows that you won’t find anywhere else, including the best Prestige TV lineup with shows like The Sopranos, The Wire, and Game of Thrones. It shows no sign of slowing down, with recent hits like The Pitt, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The White Lotus, and others reminding us why an HBO Max subscription remains non-negotiable.

Fubo has been a go-to streaming service for sports fans; there are a wide variety of cable networks, plus access to local channels and RSNs to catch games that might not be airing nationally. Beyond sports, you also get access to news, entertainment, and family channels, making it a true replacement for pricier cable packages.

While streaming services were supposed to offer greater freedom and variety, the reality is that many users find themselves toggling through nearly endless rows of options to find what to watch. Criterion brought back the sense of curation to streaming for a relatively affordable monthly price with the Criterion Channel. In addition to on-demand movies, Criterion 24/7 is the streaming service’s all-day livestream, offering a greater sense of mystery and discovery. Leave it to a physical media company to figure out what movie fans really want out of a streaming service.

Of all the streaming services out there, none quite captures the magic of childhood like Disney+. Its library is packed with hundreds of beloved Disney classics, all available on demand without having to dig out an old VHS player. And with live TV options for the adults in the household, there’s something for everyone to enjoy, all for a relatively reasonable monthly price.

Amazon’s latest Fire TV Stick delivers improved performance for ultra-high-definition TVs and a new, more intuitive interface to quickly find the content you want. The new stick also supports Wi-Fi 6 for faster 4K streaming. In short, the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus is all about speed, which is a win in our book.

Tidal has been a go-to hi-fi music streaming service for over a decade, but it’s having a moment. By taking a stance on AI-generated music, including labeling and demonetizing it, the streaming service upped its bona fides as the artist-friendly music streamer. And while it still has some of the highest resolution audio available on streaming and the highest payouts for musicians, it’s managed to do so while keeping the subscription price competitive.

Every year, Rolling Stone editors review hundreds of products and services to separate the standouts from the noise. We put brands to work in the real world, evaluating utility, creativity, design, and performance. We’re looking for companies and products that bring something new to the table: A fresh take on a familiar staple, an unexpected piece of gear we didn’t know we needed, or just something plain cool. Only a select few earn our ultimate seal of approval: A spot in the Rolling Stone Essentials Awards.

#3347. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

There are many reasons why someone might use a VPN, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

When you connect to a VPN server in the United States, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the U.S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U.S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U.S. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

If you’ve encountered something similar with your VPN provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

IP geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99.8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Websites can also use more than just your IP address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

WebRTC is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

But the catch with WebRTC is that it exposes both your VPN server and ISP-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real IP location and cause websites to reject your VPN server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Even when a browser isn’t leaking your real IP address, DNS resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

If you toggle on DNS leak protection in your VPN app, this will force websites to use your VPN’s resolver to perform DNS lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Websites rely on IP databases like Maxmind, IP2Location, IPinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

VPN providers often rely on virtual servers that use IP addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

While this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your IP address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a WebRTC or DNS issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:

We’ll start by recording your baseline IP address, country, city, and ASN. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig.co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig.co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Now connect your VPN server. Then visit IPConfig.co again to note down the changed details.

Make sure the Country and Timezone fields match your current VPN server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

In case these details do not match your VPN server, run a WebRTC leak test and a DNS leak test using BrowserLeaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

There’s no surefire way to solve IP location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

#3346. Hackers Now Want Your Browser Sessions More Than Your Passwords, but You Can Stop Them

There’s a very organized dark web supply chain that attackers use to trade in stealer logs. Russian Market has effectively replaced Genesis Market as the new storefront for black hat cybercriminals, although much of the market has also shifted to private channels on Telegram.

According to threat analysts at DarkOwl, approximately 180,000 stealer logs were sold on Russian Market in just the first half of 2025. What's more, Russian Market is a well-designed storefront that users can access even without Onion links or the Tor browser. That means anyone could go there and buy a bunch of stealer logs to start attempting account takeovers at scale.

Meanwhile, Flare Research estimates that this isn’t even close to the actual scale of the threat, because 90% of stealer logs now surface privately on Telegram. There, automated chatbots let scammers shop for stealer logs like it’s Amazon, with options to filter by country, app, and account privilege. Logs sell for anywhere between $5 and $500 a piece, depending on the estimated value of the target accounts.

The easiest way to go about this is to take a look through all your active devices and their locations in your account settings on most websites. If you see a device or location you don’t recognize, you are likely the subject of an ongoing breach. However, keep in mind that this may not always be a reliable method if you use iCloud Private Relay or a VPN. Still, it's generally best practice to log out of all active sessions every once in a while and perform a fresh login to invalidate any unauthorized sessions.

Reset the passwords on your email account, enable two-factor authentication for added protection, and sign out of all sessions before doing a fresh login. Your email inbox is the single point of entry for most attacks because that’s where most websites send their verification codes or magic links.

Sign out of all active sessions on every account that you suspect is compromised. This will log out any attackers who are currently on a hijacked browsing session.

Change your passwords on every platform in order of priority. Start with banking websites, cloud storage providers, and password managers first.

Look through each compromised account’s third-party integrations and app permissions. Revoke access if you can’t recognize an app, or it looks suspicious. Also make sure to rotate any API keys that you’re currently using, since those may have been compromised as well.

But while the initiative has already been open-sourced, no other major online provider has begun offering native support for it as of this article. That means DBSC’s security benefits are limited to Google services like Gmail and Docs, Chrome for Windows, and third-party websites that offer single sign-on (SSO) options for your Google account. We might see a wider rollout in the near future, though.

“Jesus, Mary, and Joseph and the wee donkey!”

Martin Compston, Vicky McClure and Adrian Dunbar reprise their roles as Steve Arnott, Kate Fleming and Ted Hastings, respectively in the first look at the much anticipated return of record-setting BBC cop drama Line of Duty, along with a sight of Robert Carlyle‘s character, Shaun Massie.

Season 7 of the show, which was announced in November last year amid wild speculation the ratings behemoth from Jed Mercurio series would return, will see the anti-corruption cops returning at the now rebranded Inspectorate of Professional Standards, which replaces the famous AC-12. Related Stories News James Graham's BBC Drama 'Sherwood' To End After Season 3 News Channel 4 Becomes Latest Network To Delete David Walliams Shows

There are the usual shots of the trio sat stoically in police interview rooms, along with a first look at Robert Carlyle, who is the guest lead for the series, playing Specialist Rifle Officer (SRO) Massie. Watch on Deadline

The series will explore whether the accusations made against Gough, a charismatic TO-7 officer known for a string of organized crime takedowns, is a deliberate distraction from a bigger threat lurking in the shadows.

Other actors in TO-7 team include Laura Aikman as DC Paula Beckman, Levi Brown as DC Luke Tobin, and Amy Leigh Hickman as DC Nira Rashid. Mark Bonnar, Owen Teale, Perry Fitzpatrick and Christina Chong all return to reprise their roles, with new cast members including David Calder, Steven Elder, Dominic Mafham, Aimee Powell and Naomi Yang.

Mercurio wrote and created season seven, and also directed episodes 4-6. World Productions returned to make the show in association with parent company ITV Studios, which is handling international distribution. Jennie Darnell directed the first three episodes, and the producers are Ken Horn and Richard Burnell. The executive producers are Mercurio, Simon Heath for World and Nick Lambon for the BBC. Northern Ireland Screen provided support.

#3341. Google DeepMind analysis proves Signal and WhatsApp encryption is secure

The Signal protocol has long been considered the gold standard for end-to-end encrypted messaging, with Edward Snowden a notable advocate. Now a Google DeepMind analysis has “formally verified” the security of the protocol.

In addition to its use in the Signal app, the same protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages, and the work has been described as “a landmark development” …

“Formal verification” is the term given to mathematically proving or disproving that a cryptographic algorithm or protocol satisfies its security claims under all conditions. It guarantees that there is no situation in which the protocol will fail. This is a far higher standard than traditional testing methods which seek to find vulnerabilities but cannot promise that others do not exist.

Using agentic AI to carry out formal verification is a huge breakthrough for cryptography and AI alike. It is, however, extremely computationally demanding, so Google told Wired it’s unclear as yet how practical it will be to use it more broadly.

DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process. “We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.

It’s important to note that the validation is for the protocol itself rather than the Signal app as a whole. However, encouragement can be taken from the fact that when tested against older versions of Signal that contained known vulnerabilities, it identified those and flagged them as failing formal verification.

Also worth stating is that Google was able to build on some past formal verification work already completed without the use of AI. This analysis took four weeks, and the scale of resources required has not yet been disclosed, so we shouldn’t expect a whole array of other protocols to be validated overnight. All the same, this is a very big deal.

#3337. Aura's Second E-Ink Picture Frame Is Much Improved, and Much Cheaper

Last year, Aura released the Aura Ink, its first digital photo frame using an e-ink display rather than the LCD screens common to the other devices that made them the major player in the market (Aura customers have already uploaded more than one billion photos this year alone). When I reviewed the original 13-inch Aura Ink last year, I recommended it, with a few major reservations. Today, Aura announced its second-generation 10-inch Ink frame, and while I wouldn't exactly say they've solved every one of my issues, the new device is significantly improved—and much cheaper.

Most digital photo frames will remind you of an iPad with a decorative border around it. They're great for displaying hundreds of your photos with vibrant color, but not everyone loves the look, or the fact that these frames always need to be plugged in. An e-ink frame, on the other hand, uses a variant of the sort of low-power screen you'd find in a Kindle Colorsoft—less bright, but more paperlike, and much closer to the look of a traditionally printed photo.The Aura Ink is a great choice if you want a digital frame that looks more like a "real" photo and doesn't need to be plugged in and doesn't light up like a tablet (though it does have a light, it's really to make up for the fact that color e-ink screens don't reflect light very well, and thus can make your pictures look way too dark without an additional boost). You'll still get all the benefits of an LCD frame like the Aura Aspen, including the ability to load photos from anywhere using the versatile Aura app (you can now even text them directly to the frame), but you'll only need to charge it once every few months.

Now for the downsides: Where most digital frames allow you to flick between photos with a swipe, the Aura Ink is much more sluggish—switching from one photo to another takes about 45 seconds. While an LCD can match the colors in your photo exactly, e-ink uses a "dithering algorithm" to blend tiny pixels together to create the illusion of different hues ("millions" of them, according to Aura). In practice, this means up close, your pictures will look rather grainy, and the colors won't be nearly as bright as what you see on your phone screen.

All of that said, the Aura Ink is a great product, provided you know what you're buying, and the new 10-inch model offers some big upgrades over the 13-inch original released in 2025:

Resolution has been bumped up from 150 ppi to 200 ppi, so your images look more detailed and less grainy. (Though the difference is hard to capture in a photo, I can definitely see the improvement when comparing them side-by-side.)

Instead of the six base colors available on the older frame, the 10-inch Aura Ink blends nine different hues to approximate the colors in your images, offering greater color accuracy and improved contrast.

The transition effect when you move between photos has been updated to look more intentional—like waves of color moving across the screen versus a series of increasingly intense flashes.

It's a heck of a lot cheaper: $349, versus $499 for the 13-inch model—though that's still significantly pricier than Aura's most popular offering, the 10.1-inch Aura Carver, which starts around $200 less.

I write a lot about e-ink devices, from e-readers to tablets, and my common refrain, especially with color devices, is that they're great at what they do, but you should understand what they do before you plunk down your money. The Aura Ink will never look as bright and colorful as an LCD frame, and if you want a frame that can switch between images every few minutes or even play video, you'll need to look elsewhere (to maximize battery life, Aura recommends swapping photos on the Aura Ink no more than 12 times per day).

But if you want to display photos that look more like the ones that hung on the walls of your childhood home, in a frame that doesn't need to be plugged in all the time, you'll probably dig it, provided you can stomach the $350 price tag.

#3336. Ring’s wheeled and flying robots will patrol your home

Some people use a whole bunch of fixed cameras to monitor their homes, but Amazon has just announced a more flexible solution through wheeled and flying robots.

Both the $250 Drone Cam and $1,000 Rover Cam can respond to alarms or door and window sensor alerts in order to go check out what’s happening and send live video …

Amazon says they are the first two Ring Robotics products, with more likely to follow. Both are autonomous.

Ring Drone and Ring Rover are both powered by AI Pilot, a custom-built system that uses the devices’ cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate autonomously.

AI Pilot simplifies the customer experience, starting with setup. Simply carry Ring Drone through your space or let Ring Rover autonomously explore, and it turns what it sees into a floor plan. It intelligently identifies rooms and suggests patrol points: spots worth extra attention. This could be a side door, windows, a register, or a long corridor, helping eliminate guesswork while also allowing you to add additional points customized to your space and security preferences.

When a patrol or flight is initiated, AI Pilot plans the most efficient route to get to a preset point based on the map it’s created. From there, it reacts in real time—autonomously navigating around furniture, shelving, and any obstacle it encounters.

You can set either device to patrol on a fixed schedule, as well as activate them manually, but they will also automatically respond to sensor alerts and alarms.

When a Ring camera, sensor, or alarm is triggered, [either device] automatically [moves] to previously set patrol points to investigate […] Continuous person motion detection means Ring Rover can alert you and start recording the moment it detects motion in its view—even when docked.

The Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping on December 16 for $999.99, but you can preorder it today. The Drone Cam starts shipping in late January for $249.99, but there’s no preorder yet.

#3334. Adobe unveils new AI tools for Photoshop, Premiere, and more, with MCP support coming in 2027

Adobe today announced a sweeping set of updates at its annual Adobe MAX conference, focused on giving users more ways to automate complex workflows, edit content, and work across its creative apps. Here are the details.

At the Adobe MAX event today, the company unveiled a series of features, many of them AI-powered or AI-assisted, that will begin rolling out across its suite of creative platforms as early as today.

In Photoshop, the new Relight tool offers a way to non-destructively and dynamically add, reposition, and resize light sources in the composition, while Generative Restylelets users** prompt the platform to generate variations of an image’s style and fine-tune the results using adjustable sliders.

Photoshop is also adding a Quick Compare slider to make it easier to track before-and-after results, and is getting several features in the beta app, including, per Adobe:

Following its acquisition of Topaz Labs, Adobe is also introducing two new AI image enhancement models: Wonder 4, which combines upscaling, denoising, deblurring, and sharpening into a single operation, and Image HDR, which converts standard images into HDR with improved brightness and detail.

Adobe Premiere is also getting generative tools that make it easier to prepare raw files for a project, including Enhance Audio, Separate Crosstalk, and Separate Sound Source. Adobe is also adding a Generative Remove tool to Premiere in beta, “bringing you the power to remove unwanted objects, like boom mics and logos or background distractions, directly on your timeline,” says the company.

Premiere is also getting Color Mode, a new color-grading tool starting today, which “supports everything from quick corrections to more advanced grades while keeping your video as the focus.”

Another interesting tool making its way into Premiere is Generative Media Tool. Here’s Adobe:

The Generative Media Tool brings Generate Video, Generate Sound Effects, Generate Soundscape and Generate Music directly into your timeline in Premiere. You can generate missing b-roll, background music or sound for a scene using context from your edit, then keep refining the result in your timeline. You can also choose from Adobe Firefly and models from partners including Google, Kling, Runway and Luma based on the creative needs of your project.

As for iPhone users who rely on Premiere Mobile, Adobe announced that its newly established partnerships with UMG and WMG will bring hundreds of thousands of licensed music tracks to the app (for non-commercial use) starting today, with users able to explore trending songs, discover featured artists, and create videos using artist-inspired templates.

Premiere mobile is also getting agentic tools soon, including Quick Cuts, which generates a first cut based on the user’s prompt and the materials they add, and an AI Assistant, which helps users find the right editing tools and execute tasks based on natural language instructions.

In Lightroom, the company is adding multiple new tools that make it easier to edit or more quickly fix small imperfections. That includes Glow, which “adds soft, cinematic light to your photos,” Blemish Removal for quick skin fine-tuning, Open Eyes in beta, and an improved and expanded Camera Tethering on Desktop and the iPad, with support for more cameras and advanced shooting controls, plus the ability to connect cameras directly to an iPad for live previews and photo editing.

Adobe is adding new brushes, gradients, patterns, and graphic styles to Illustrator, alongside new Blend controls, which “make it easier to develop and refine designs with a persistent control panel and live preview,” per the company.

As for InDesign, a new Co-editing feature, available in beta, streamlines collaborative work, while the new Flex Layout tool dynamically adjusts content based on the canvas size and artwork. InDesign is also getting Check Document and Rewrite that more quickly “help identify common editorial and accessibility issues while you’re still working.”

While it will not launch until 2027, this feature will enable users to connect Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects to the AI tools and agents they already use.

In practice, this will mean connecting Photoshop to ChatGPT and having them work in tandem to adapt an entire campaign based on new artwork you develop and attach to your prompt.

This integration will also account for other connected tools, so the user can ask ChatGPT to make edits, add new files to a Google Drive folder, update the team on Slack, and so on.

Here’s Adobe on the upcoming MCP integration:

Because it runs locally on your computer, your agent works directly in your native project files, and your layers, vectors, bins and sequences stay editable.

The company notes that MCP integrations will enter private beta in early 2027, and users can sign up here to learn more.

According to Adobe, Firefly is getting even better at helping users organize and edit their raw material for tasks such as turning travel clips into a vlog, creating social media campaigns, or assembling videos from storyboards.

The new Firefly Video lets users organize scenes, assemble clips, add captions, and generate transitions and B-roll, while Firefly Design brings illustration, image editing, animation, and 3D tools into a single canvas.

Adobe is also adding Quick Actions for common editing tasks, Firefly Graph for creating reusable workflows, and Firefly Builder (in private beta) for prototyping websites and apps using natural language.

Firefly’s AI Assistant is also getting new capabilities, including Plan Mode, which lets users review and approve an agent’s proposed actions, and Model Selector, which lets them choose which AI model to use.

Adobe is also previewing Always-on agents, which can handle recurring tasks such as organizing assets, checking quality, and preparing content for different platforms in the background, even when users step away.

Adobe is also expanding its Creative Agent across Creative Cloud, with AI Assistants now available in beta in Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign, After Effects, and Frame.io, as well as the Photoshop beta app.

These assistants allow users to execute complex, multi-step tasks using natural language prompts. In Premiere, for example, users can ask the assistant to apply effects to an entire sequence, track subjects across frames, or adjust color and exposure across multiple clips.

To learn more about these and other features announced at Adobe MAX today, stay tuned to the company’s blog.

EXCLUSIVE: BBC Director General Matt Brittin is one of a number of industry bosses who will attend an emergency meeting convened by the UK Culture Secretary next week in the wake of the Russell Brand, David Walliams and MAFS scandals.

Nandy will tell a meeting of leaders that if their response to the recent allegations is not robust enough, she may consider introducing legislation to force them to fund the just-launched CIISA anonymous whistleblowing service.

Earlier today, she told parliament: “I want to be clear that if protections are insufficient, the government will not hesitate to take further action. For too long, too many people have had to choose between their careers and safety. People must be safe in their jobs, whistleblowers must be protected and those who abuse their position must no longer be able to hide.” Related Stories News 'Line Of Duty': Arnott, Fleming & Hastings Return To Service In First Look At Season 7 Of BBC's Record-Setting Cop Drama News Meta Removes Russell Brand's Instagram & Facebook Account After Rape Conviction

Deadline is told invitations to attend Nandy’s meeting landed with the big broadcasters and Sky yesterday. BBC DG Brittin will almost definitely attend, we understand. Others are considering who will attend from their organizations but it would be no surprise if they send their most senior individual, especially if Brittin goes. Earlier this week, Brittin emailed all BBC employees with title “Building the culture we want” to say “there is still more to do to engage with staff and represent their views” to try and stamp these problems out. He said he will be speaking to trade unions about changes that could be made immediately and in the next charter. Deadline understands Phillipa Childs, who runs broadcasting union Bectu, will attend Nandy’s meeting. Watch on Deadline

We are told the Nandy meeting could happen as soon as Monday. She has made cleaning up the TV industry’s bad behavior problem one of the cornerstones of her time as Culture Secretary and has been enraged by the latest high-profile examples.

Nandy’s idea is that the big networks and production groups could be forced to fund CIISA each year. This is not a new argument. Deadline revealed nearly two years ago, before CIISA was up and running properly, that Nandy was considering legislation that would force UK broadcasters to regularly fund the body, which emerged from the Noel Clarke scandal and Time’s Up UK movement.

The whistleblowing service opened a few weeks ago in earnest but regular donations are required to keep it running, especially if there is an influx of complaints following these high-profile allegations. The body would also like to expand its scope at some point to areas like arbitration. CIISA representatives have been invited to Nandy’s meeting and we understand CIISA will host an event in parliament later this month.

CIISA has indicated that running costs would be around £1.5M ($2M) in its first year, rising to just more than £2M the following one to fund its small team and operations. The body has floated a funding model based on organizations paying an ongoing yearly contribution of a maximum 0.1% of their annual turnover. Current financial backers include the likes of the BBC, ITV, Sky and big production groups.

Nandy and other senior government ministers are also focused on non-disclosure agreements, with Bridget Phillipson, the UK’s womens and equalities minister, telling Sky News such agreements should not be “abused in order to silence women.”

All this has contributed to a feeling within the industry that enough is enough.

An open letter has been doing the rounds, signed by dozens of actors, writers and directors, which is titled “Let’s make this a turning point” and urges industry action.

“We call on every union, every company and every industry organisation to stop enabling a systemic cycle of abuse, whether through unconscious inaction or deliberate distraction,” it reads. “Review your processes. Protect those who speak out. Become less offended by your inaction being named than you are by the actions you are being asked to recognise.”

Brand was sentenced earlier this week to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault and the TV industry has been heavily implicated, with one of the women he sexually assaulted working for Channel 4 at the time. Earlier this week, The Guardian and ITV News published allegations against of sexually exploitative activity against women and girls from Walliams, allegations that he denies. Meanwhile, Channel 4 axed Married at First Sight last week after rape allegations.

You can set price alerts for products you want and your Alexa devices can notify you when they go on sale.

There are usually some invite-only deals that you can sign up for.

There are tools you can use to see if the deal you're looking at is worthwhile or not.

But if you only take one bit of advice for shopping on Amazon, let it be this one: Don't buy anything you weren't going to buy anyway. A good way to make sure you do this is by making a list of the products you do want, and only having eyes for those.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you, and don’t stress over finding the perfect timing.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but prices aren’t always what they seem. Use a price tracker to make sure you’re getting the best deal, or refer to guides like our live blog that use price trackers for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: Think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that you're less likely to see throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech.
